# A ternary in a timer's @tick does not take the build down.
#
# The goldens in testdata/timer_tick_lowered.txtar pin the shape this lowers
# to. What they cannot say is how it failed: `ir.Ternary reached Go codegen`
# is a panic in the Go emitter, not a diagnostic, so the build died with a
# stack trace and no position. Only a harness that runs the CLI can assert an
# exit status and the absence of that text.
#
# The @click control is here because it is what isolated the position: the
# identical body in a click handler always lowered, so the constructs were
# never the problem.

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea --out tick tick.sngl
! stderr 'reached Go codegen'
! stderr 'goroutine 1 \[running\]'
exists tick/model.go

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea --out click click.sngl
exists click/model.go

# And the schedule is in the tree the dump prints, which is what lets the
# lowering have one path for it. It used to be lifted onto its owner by a pass
# of its own, into a list the dump did not print for a window at all -- so the
# stage after the lift showed no timer anywhere. The gate is printed with it:
# `enabled` is the primitive's own prop, and nothing wrote one here.
sngl dump --stage lowered --after Effect --lang go --platform bubbletea tick.sngl
stdout 'Timer\(interval=50ms, enabled=true, @tick \{'

-- tick.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea
    }
}

component ticker ui.node {
    var level = 0.0

    time.timer(interval=50ms, @tick {
        level = level >= 1 ? 0.0 : level + 0.01
    })

    ui.text(value="{level}")
}

ui.window #main(title="tick") {
    ticker()
}
-- click.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea
    }
}

component clicker ui.node {
    var level = 0.0

    ui.button(text="step", @click {
        level = level >= 1 ? 0.0 : level + 0.01
    })

    ui.text(value="{level}")
}

ui.window #main(title="click") {
    clicker()
}
